The app read and wrote server settings through **two different preference files**:

| Code path | File used |
|---|---|
| `ServerSettingsFragment` / `SettingsFragment` (the settings UI) | `PreferenceManager.getDefaultSharedPreferences()` → **`<applicationId>_preferences`** |
| `Util.getPreferences()` (used by the rest of the app, incl. `MusicServiceFactory`) | hardcoded **`"org.moire.ultrasonic_preferences"`** |

`ultrasonic/build.gradle` applies `applicationIdSuffix ".debug"` to debug builds, so the debug app's default preference file is `org.moire.ultrasonic.debug_preferences` — **a completely different file** from the hardcoded `org.moire.ultrasonic_preferences`.

So the URL/username/password the user typed were saved into the default file, but `MusicServiceFactory.createSubsonicApiClient()` looked them up in the hardcoded file, found `null`, and hit its fallback branch:

```java
if (serverUrl == null || username == null || password == null) {
    Log.i("MusicServiceFactory", "Server credentials is not available");
    return new SubsonicAPIClient("http://localhost", "", "", ...);
```

which is exactly the `Failed to connect to localhost/127.0.0.1:80` in the reported stack trace. This also explains why 2.2.2 worked: in a *release* build `getPackageName()` is `org.moire.ultrasonic`, making the two names coincidentally identical, so the mismatch only surfaced on the `master` debug build the reporter was testing.

## The fix

Made `Util.getPreferences()` the single source of truth, returning the same default preference file the `PreferenceFragment`-based settings screens use, and routed the two fragments and `getActiveServers()` through it. The now-unused, misleading `Constants.PREFERENCES_FILE_NAME` was removed so the hardcoded name can't be reintroduced.

Importantly, this fix is **migration-safe**: for release builds the default preference name resolves to `org.moire.ultrasonic_preferences`, byte-for-byte the old hardcoded value, so existing users lose no settings.

## Verification

A real `./gradlew clean assembleDebug` cannot complete in this environment: the machine has no network (blocked even with the sandbox disabled), and `com.twitter.serial:serial:0.1.6` and `org.jetbrains.kotlin:kotlin-stdlib-common:1.2.51` are absent from every local Gradle cache. This is a pre-existing dependency-resolution limitation in the untouched `dependencies.gradle` — unrelated to source changes. I did get the build to progress through 22 executed tasks by assembling a local Maven mirror from the cached artifacts before hitting those two missing ones.

To verify compilation regardless, I ran a **differential `javac` compile** of the whole `ultrasonic` Java source set against `android-27` plus a classpath built from every cached jar/AAR, comparing the original sources to the patched ones:

- original: 2596 errors, patched: 2596 errors
- Error sets (file + message, line numbers normalized) are **byte-identical** — the only raw difference was line-number shifts in `Util.java` from my added comment.

All 2596 are pre-existing `package org.moire.ultrasonic.domain does not exist`-style errors caused by Kotlin/sibling-module classes missing from that ad-hoc classpath, not by the patch. So the change introduces no compile errors, and it is confined to four Java files with no build-script or resource changes.
